'''thrush-babbler''' (thrush′bab″lėr), ''n.'' Any babbling thrush: same as ''babbler'', 2.

{{smaller block|The feeble-winged ''thrush-babblers'' were wrangling over worms.
{{right|''P. Robinson'', Under the Sun, p. 79.}}}}

'''thrush-blackbird''' (thrush′blak″bėrd), ''n.'' The rusty grackle, ''Scolecophagus ferrugineus.'' {{smaller|This bird is not obviously different from some thrushes in form, and in its varying plumages was repeatedly described as different species of the genus ''Turdus.'' See cut under ''rusty.''}}

'''thrushel''' (thrush′l), ''n.'' [See ''throstle'' (''f'').] Same as ''throstle.'' [Prov. Eng.]

'''thrusher''' (thrush′ėr), ''n.'' [Appar. a var. of ''thrushel'', with accom. term. ''-er.'' Hence prob., as another var., ''thrasher''<sup>2</sup>, q. v.] Same as ''thrush''<sup>1</sup>; specifically, the song-thrush, ''Turdus musicus.'' See cut under ''thrush''<sup>1</sup>.

'''thrush-fungus''' (thrush′fung″gus), ''n.'' The fungus ''Saccharomyces albicans'', which produces the disease in man known as ''thrush.''

'''thrushil†''', ''n.'' An obsolete form of ''thrushel.''

'''thrush-lichen''' (thrush′lī″ken), ''n.'' A lichen, the ''Peltigera aphthosa'', which grows on moist alpine rocks. The Swedes boil it in milk as a cure for thrush (whence the name).

'''thrush-nightingale''' (thrush′nī″tin-gāl), ''n.'' See ''nightingale''<sup>1</sup>, 1.

'''thrush-paste''' (thrush′pāst), ''n.'' An astringent for curing thrush in the feet of horses. It is composed of calamin, verdigris, white vitriol, alum, and tar.

'''thrush-tit''' (thrush′tit), ''n.'' A book-name of those turdoid oscine birds of the Himalayan region,

China, and Java which belong to a genus named ''Cochoa'' by Hodgson in 1836 (changed to ''Prosorinia'' by him in 1844, and renamed ''Xanthogenys'' by Cabanis in 1850). {{smaller|These birds are neither thrushes nor tits, and are scattered widely through the ornithological system by various taxonomists. The 3 species are very beautiful. ''C. viridis'' and ''C. purpurea'' (each 11 inches long) inhabit parts of the Himalayas and China; ''C. azurea'' (9 inches) inhabits Java. Their coloration is indicated with some accuracy in their respective specific names.}}

'''thrust'''<sup>1</sup> (thrust), ''v.''; pret. and pp. ''thrust'', ppr. ''thrusting''. [< ME. ''thrusten'', but usually ''thresten'', ''thristen'', < Icel. ''thrȳsta'', thrust, press, force, compel; ult. connected with ''threat'', q. v.] '''I.''' ''trans.''
